title: The Oracle at Delphi
objective: After this level you can explain how the Oracle advised cities and kings.
summary: At Delphi the Pythia spoke for Apollo; colonists, cities and kings consulted her, and her ambiguous answers could mislead, as Croesus learned.

cards.headline: A king asked Delphi about war. The answer was true, and it ruined him.
cards.body: That’s the story of Croesus and the Greek world’s great advice service. Cities, colonists and kings all lined up to ask.

cards.headline: Ask Apollo
cards.body: At Delphi, in the mountains of central Greece, a prophetess called the Pythia spoke the will of the god Apollo, seated on a sacred tripod. The oracle worked only a limited number of days, and generous donors could jump to the head of the line. Even divine advice, it turns out, had a VIP queue.

cards.headline: Advice for cities
cards.body: Greeks planning a new colony most often asked Apollo at Delphi for approval first. Remember Level 9’s colonies? Delphi’s blessing was part of the send-off. And in Level 13, Cypselus took Corinth with a favorable oracle from Delphi. A yes from Apollo was a powerful thing to have on your side.

cards.headline: Read the small print
cards.body: Priests wrote the answers down in verse that was often highly ambiguous. Herodotus tells how Croesus of Lydia, the kingdom that made the first coins, asked whether to attack Persia. He would destroy a great empire, came the reply. He attacked, and the empire he destroyed was his own. Treat it as a story Greeks loved to tell, not a transcript.

mascot.line: Delphi’s answers were often ambiguous. Lesson: always ask a follow-up question.

cards.headline: Delphi: consulted
learned: The Pythia spoke for Apollo at Delphi
Croesus destroyed a great empire: his own

questions.prompt: At the Oracle of Delphi, who spoke Apollo’s answers?

options.label: A priest of Zeus from Olympia
options.rationale: Olympia was Zeus’s sanctuary; Delphi was Apollo’s.

questions.explanation: The Pythia, seated on a sacred tripod, spoke the will of Apollo.

questions.prompt: Why did Croesus’s famous answer from Delphi prove disastrous for him?

options.label: The oracle told him never to fight
options.rationale: It said he would destroy a great empire.

options.label: He never received any answer
options.rationale: He did, and acted on it.

options.label: It was ambiguous: the great empire was his own
The Pythia secretly worked for Persia
options.rationale: The words were true, just ambiguous.

questions.explanation: Delphi’s answers were often ambiguous; Croesus destroyed an empire, his own.

questions.prompt: Level 9’s Greeks founded colonies around the sea. What did colony founders most often do before setting out?

options.label: Ask Apollo at Delphi for approval
Mint coins with a turtle stamp

questions.explanation: Greeks planning a colony most often sought Apollo’s approval at Delphi first.
